header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Using individual neurons as these units has had some success (Olah et al., 2020; Bills et al., 2023), but a key challenge has been that neurons are almost always polysemantic, with nearly every neuron activating for several unrelated types of feature (Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

events.delta:
Verdict: not supported, at least as worded.

The cited Olah et al. (2020) source, Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits, supports that neurons are often polysemantic, but not that they are "almost always" or "nearly every neuron" polysemantic.

- "Neural networks often contain “polysemantic neurons” that respond to multiple unrelated inputs. For example, InceptionV1 contains one neuron that responds to cat faces, fronts of cars, and cat legs." (distill:zoom-in/r1/b62)
- "polysemantic neurons are a major challenge for the circuits agenda, significantly limiting our ability to reason about neural networks." (distill:zoom-in/r1/b65)

The source says "often," not "almost always," and gives no evidence that nearly every neuron is polysemantic. The source does support the "key challenge" part.

Bills et al. (2023) is not in the library, so the "some success" claim attributed to it could not be checked.

The exact sentence could not be located in any library document. The closest is Cunningham et al., Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models (arxiv:2309.08600/v3/p2), which cites Bills et al. for autointerpretability scores but does not contain the quoted sentence.

Suggested correction: "Using individual neurons as these units has had some success (Olah et al., 2020; Bills et al., 2023), but a key challenge is that neurons are often polysemantic, responding to multiple unrelated inputs (Olah et al., 2020)."
